data.body_html:
When planning a boat rental on the Costa del Sol, the first decision is often: Marbella vs Sotogrande – which departure point wins? Both are glamorous, but they offer very different experiences. Our fleet, based in Puerto Banús (Marbella), gives you immediate access to the liveliest marina on the coast, while Sotogrande offers a quieter, more exclusive vibe. In this guide, we break down the pros and cons of each, so you can choose the perfect starting point for your charter.

Puerto Banús: The Heart of Marbella's Luxury

Puerto Banús is more than a marina – it's a destination in itself. Located just 8 km from Marbella centre and about 45 minutes from Málaga airport, it's the easiest place to start a charter. The marina is packed with designer boutiques, Michelin-starred restaurants, and some of the world's most impressive superyachts. When you step aboard our Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39, you're literally minutes from the action.

From Puerto Banús, you can cruise to the Golden Mile, anchor off the Marbella Club, or head to quieter spots like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. The choice is yours – and you don't waste time getting there.

Sotogrande: Exclusive and Serene

Sotogrande, about 80 km from Málaga airport (1h 15m drive), is a private residential resort known for its golf courses (Valderrama, La Reserva) and polo fields. It's quieter, more understated, and attracts a crowd that values privacy over spectacle. If you're looking to escape the crowds and enjoy a peaceful day on the water, Sotogrande has its charms – but it's a different kind of luxury.

However, Sotogrande doesn't have the same concentration of charter boats or services. You'll find fewer options, and the marina is more functional than glamorous. For most visitors, the extra drive and limited fleet make it a less practical choice.

Distance and Travel Time: Which Is More Convenient?

FactorPuerto Banús (Marbella)Sotogrande
From Málaga airport45 min (50 km)1h 15m (80 km)
From Marbella centre10 min45 min

If you're based in Marbella or staying on the Golden Mile, Puerto Banús is a no-brainer. If you're in Sotogrande, you could still drive to Puerto Banús – it's a 45-minute scenic drive – and enjoy a far wider choice of boats and itineraries.

Cost Comparison: What You Pay for a Charter

Our pricing is transparent and includes everything: licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). For a Tier A boat (Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39), you pay €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. That's a full day with no hidden extras.

For a larger group, the Mangusta 80 (white or grey) starts at €4,719 for 4 hours, and that includes a free jet ski. Other boats – like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86 – are priced on request via WhatsApp. In Sotogrande, you'll likely pay similar rates, but with fewer boats to choose from and often less inclusive packages.

Itineraries: What You Can See from Each Base

From Puerto Banús, you can head east to Cabopino (a charming fishing village with a sandy beach) or west to Estepona (about 20 nm, perfect for a full-day cruise). The coastline between Marbella and Estepona is dotted with hidden coves like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, ideal for swimming and snorkelling.

From Sotogrande, the coast is less developed. You can visit the beaches of San Roque or head towards Gibraltar, but the scenery is less varied. For most charter guests, the flexibility of Puerto Banús is a huge advantage – you can tailor your day to your mood, whether that's beach-hopping or anchoring for a long lunch.

The Social Scene: Marina Life Matters

Part of the boat rental experience is the marina itself. Puerto Banús buzzes with energy – you can sip a cocktail at a beach club before boarding, and after your trip, enjoy dinner at one of the many waterfront restaurants. The marina is a people-watching paradise, with celebrities and superyachts around every corner.

Sotogrande is more about tranquillity. It's perfect if you want to unwind, but if you're looking for a lively day out, it might feel a bit sleepy. Our advice: start in Puerto Banús, and if you want a quiet anchorage, we'll take you to one – you get the best of both worlds.

Our Fleet: Departing from Puerto Banús

All 17 boats in our fleet depart from Puerto Banús. From the compact Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) to the majestic Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax), we have a boat for every occasion. Popular choices include the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) and the Fairline Targa 12m (10 pax). Every charter includes a professional skipper, so you can relax and enjoy the ride.

If you're planning a group celebration, the Mangusta 80 is a showstopper – 24 metres of Italian style, with a free jet ski for extra fun. For a more intimate trip, the Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) is perfect for a quick spin to Cabopino.

Making the Choice: Which Is Right for You?

Choose Puerto Banús if you want:

  • Easy access from Málaga airport and Marbella centre.
  • A wide range of boats and inclusive pricing.
  • A lively marina with dining and nightlife.
  • Flexible itineraries to Cabopino, Estepona, and hidden coves.

Choose Sotogrande if you want:

  • A quieter, more exclusive atmosphere.
  • Proximity to top golf courses (if you're combining with a round).
  • A low-key day away from crowds.

But remember: you can always drive to Puerto Banús from Sotogrande in under an hour. Our team can help you plan the perfect day, whether you're celebrating a birthday, a corporate event, or just want to soak up the sun. Browse our fleet and see which boat suits your group.
